security.note: No own ir.model.access / ir.rule rows: the module ships no new stored model (8 inherit-only extensions). Access is governed by the parent models' security (delivery.carrier, stock.warehouse, sale.order, payment.* under website_sale_stock / delivery / payment). Storefront routes are auth='public' (website public user), back-office config is reached through res.config.settings / Website settings (website group_website_designer/publisher).

views.note: 6 view XML files (483 XML LOC), all view-inherit (no new act_window/menu): a stock.warehouse form extension adding opening_hours, a delivery.carrier form/list for in_store config (Stores, excluded tags), res.config.settings (eCommerce Shipping > Click & Collect toggle + action button), stock.picking, and storefront QWeb (templates.xml / delivery_form_templates.xml) for the in-store delivery option and pickup-address block. The 'list:1' counted is the in_store delivery-carrier list.

behavioral_notes.observation: Two jsonrpc/public routes drive store selection. (1) website_sale_get_pickup_locations (bare @route(), so it keeps the parent path /website_sale/get_pickup_locations) is overridden so that when opened from a PRODUCT page (kwargs['product_id']) it first forces the in-store method onto the order: if request.cart exists and its carrier is not in_store it calls order.set_delivery_line(in_store_dm, in_store_dm.product_id.list_price); if there is NO cart it builds a transient sale.order.new({'carrier_id': in_store_dm.id}) and returns its pickup locations WITHOUT creating a cart. It then calls super(), which dispatches reflectively to _{delivery_type}_get_close_locations = delivery.carrier._in_store_get_close_locations: that method geo_localizes the partner address (base_geolocalize), iterates warehouse_ids, builds each store's _prepare_pickup_location_data() payload, attaches per-store in_store_stock_data, computes the Haversine distance via utils.calculate_partner_distance(partner, wh.partner_id) and returns the stores SORTED BY DISTANCE. (2) /shop/set_click_and_collect_location (new route, called by the product-page widget) does request.cart or request.website._create_cart(), forces the in_store carrier via set_delivery_line if needed, then order._set_pickup_location(pickup_location_data). It is deliberately distinct from website_sale's /website_sale/set_pickup_location, which is only used on the checkout page after the delivery method is already chosen. Not visible in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: warehouse + fiscal-position selection from the chosen store (models/sale_order.py _set_pickup_location / _compute_warehouse_id / _compute_fiscal_position_id / _set_delivery_method)
behavioral_notes.observation: Picking a store rewires the order. _set_pickup_location() (override) stores pickup_location_data = json.loads(...) and, for in_store carriers, sets self.warehouse_id = pickup_location_data['id'] (the warehouse IS the pickup point) then _compute_fiscal_position_id(). _compute_warehouse_id() is overridden to SKIP recomputation for in_store orders that already have pickup data (otherwise super() would override the user's store choice) and instead pins warehouse_id to the picked store. _compute_fiscal_position_id() is overridden so tax is computed against the STORE's address (delivery=order.warehouse_id.partner_id) rather than the customer's shipping address, so in-store taxes are the store's. _set_delivery_method() detects a transition OUT of in_store (was in_store, new method isn't) and re-runs _compute_warehouse_id + _compute_fiscal_position_id to undo the store pinning. Not visible in metadata.

Availability is computed per candidate warehouse using product.with_context(warehouse_id=wh.id).free_qty. website._get_product_available_qty (override) returns: the SELECTED store's stock when an in_store pickup location is chosen; otherwise max(website-warehouse stock, _get_max_in_store_product_available_qty) = the best stock across all in_store warehouses, so the product page can show 'available in store' before any store is picked. product.template._get_additionnal_combination_info injects show_click_and_collect_availability (true when Click&Collect is enabled, the variant is_storable, and not excluded by the carrier's excluded_tag_ids) plus delivery_stock_data and in_store_stock_data into the storefront combination info (the ClickAndCollectAvailability OWL widget reads these). sale.order._get_insufficient_stock_data groups order lines by product, compares free_qty (rounded DOWN to integer) against ordered qty in the line UoM, and on shortage sets ol.shop_warning '%(available_qty)s/%(line_qty)s available at this location'; _is_in_stock(wh_id) = no insufficient-stock data. Not visible in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: delivery.carrier in_store type + publish/warehouse defaults (models/delivery_carrier.py) and website.in_store_dm_id resolution
behavioral_notes.observation: delivery_type gets a selection_add ('in_store', 'Pick up in store') with ondelete set default; warehouse_ids (Stores M2M to stock.warehouse) is the pickup-point catalog. create()/write() force in_store defaults via _get_in_store_default_vals() (integration_level='rate' -- rate only, never rate_and_ship; allow_cash_on_delivery=False; clears country_ids/state_ids/zip_prefix_ids so geographic delivery filters don't apply), and on create auto-fills warehouse_ids with all company warehouses and is_published = bool(warehouses). @api.constrains block publishing an in_store method with no warehouse and forbid warehouses from a different company. in_store_rate_shipment returns a flat price = carrier.product_id.list_price (the Click&Collect 'shipping' fee). website.in_store_dm_id is a COMPUTED field: it searches published in_store carriers and filters to the website's company/website scope, [:1] -- this single computed carrier is the gate every other override checks (request.website.sudo().in_store_dm_id). Not visible in metadata.

'Pay on site' is payment_custom with custom_mode='on_site'. _get_compatible_providers (override) only offers the on_site custom provider when the order's carrier is in_store AND the order has a physical ('consu') product, else it filters the provider out and records reason 'no in-store delivery methods available' in the availability report. _validate_transaction_for_order (controller override) hard-guards the inverse: paying with the on_site custom provider while the carrier is NOT in_store raises ValidationError ('You can only pay on site when selecting the pick up in store delivery method') -- defence against a forged request. The completion itself is payment.transaction._post_process (override): for on_site txs in state 'pending' it takes their draft sale orders and calls .with_context(send_email=True).action_confirm() -- i.e. an on-site order is CONFIRMED (and its stock.picking created, confirmation email sent) on a PENDING transaction, because the cash is collected later at the counter; there is no captured online payment. post_init_hook/uninstall_hook call setup_provider/reset_payment_provider(env,'custom',custom_mode='on_site'). Not visible in metadata.

6 JS files, 1 OWL component (ClickAndCollectAvailability, registered as a public_component on the product page), 5 patches (Checkout.prototype, LocationSelectorDialog + .prototype, PaymentForm.prototype, WebsiteSale.prototype) and 2 web_tour tours; 1 web.assets_frontend bundle ('website_sale_collect/static/src/**/*'). The store-picker UX is delivered as a website public component that opens @delivery's LocationSelectorDialog (map + list, patched here for the product-page/frontend case) and, on save, posts the chosen store to /shop/set_click_and_collect_location; it listens on env.bus 'updateCombinationInfo' to refresh in_store/delivery stock badges when the variant changes. No backend OWL views.

Reserve-and-Collect (pay on site): confirm order on a pending on_site transaction -> stock.picking created at the chosen store -> customer pays and collects at the counter

stock.warehouse (pickup point with opening_hours and geo address)

cannot pay / cannot proceed if a storable product is short at the selected store (_check_cart_is_ready_to_be_paid, _get_shop_payment_errors)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_sale_collect inherits the value logic of its website_sale(_stock) parent: it is an omnichannel eCommerce FULFILMENT OPTION bolted onto the online sell-side channel, so value_model is network (Stabell & Fjeldstad). Its work is mediation over shared channel infrastructure -- matching a shopper to a nearby store (geolocated, distance-sorted, stock-aware) and binding the storefront cart to a specific warehouse and a pay-on-site provider -- not the linear transform-inputs-to-output of a chain. It owns no document/order chain of its own: it decorates website_sale's sale.order cart (pins warehouse_id + fiscal position, adds the in_store carrier) and hands off to the existing flow (action_confirm -> stock.picking via stock; on_site cash leg via payment_custom). Activity is primary because it is a revenue- and customer-facing channel/fulfilment capability on the sell side, hence APQC 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (it extends the eCommerce sell channel with a click-and-collect option), matching the website_sale / website_sale_wishlist family. A secondary OUTBOUND-LOGISTICS / order-fulfilment facet is real -- it selects the fulfilling warehouse and triggers the pickup picking, which touches APQC 4.x Deliver Physical Products (notably 4.4 outbound transportation/ship, here a customer-collect variant) -- but that fulfilment is executed by the underlying stock / delivery / sale_stock chain, not by this add-on, so 3.0 (sell channel) is primary and 4.4 (deliver) is a downstream facet, not the home category.
classification.apqc_secondary_facet: 4.4 Operate outbound logistics / order fulfilment (Deliver Physical Products) -- in-store-collect variant; executed by stock/delivery, triggered here.

standard_capabilities: In-store pickup ('Pick up in store') as a published delivery method backed by one or more warehouses
Geolocated, distance-sorted store selector (map + list) reachable from the product page and from checkout
Per-store, per-variant stock availability badges on the storefront (in-store vs ship-from-warehouse)
Order warehouse and fiscal position automatically set from the chosen store
Pay on site (cash at counter) provider, restricted to in-store orders with physical goods
Order confirmed (picking created) on a pending on-site transaction for later in-store payment
Store opening-hours and address shown in the picker; single-store auto-selection
typical_fits: Retailer with physical shops offering buy-online / collect-in-store on the eCommerce site
Multi-warehouse company exposing several stores as pickup points (distance-ranked)
Reserve-and-pay-at-counter (no online payment) using the built-in 'Pay on site' provider
Single-store merchant where the one store is auto-selected for every Click&Collect order
common_gaps: Pickup time-slot / appointment booking and capacity per store (opening hours are display-only)
Store-level reservation/hold of stock between order and collection (relies on standard stock reservation at confirm)
Partial fulfilment / split between in-store-available and to-be-shipped lines in one order
Real distance/driving time or external store-locator API (uses Haversine + OpenStreetMap geocoding only)
Click&Collect-specific notifications (ready-for-pickup SMS/email beyond the standard confirmation email)
drive_hints: odoo shell: w = env['website'].get_current_website(); w.sudo().in_store_dm_id  # the computed Click&Collect carrier for the site
curl jsonrpc /shop/set_click_and_collect_location {pickup_location_data: <json store>}  # set in_store method + store on the cart (auth=public)

open_questions: Exact stock semantics between order confirmation and collection: whether the pending on_site action_confirm reserves stock at the chosen warehouse (standard stock reservation) or only creates the picking, and how oversell at the counter is handled.
How a mixed cart (some lines in stock at the store, some not) is meant to be resolved at checkout -- the code blocks payment on any shortage rather than splitting shipped vs collected lines.
Whether opening_hours / store capacity feed any pickup-scheduling beyond display, and how express-checkout (which excludes in_store methods) interacts with a customer who wanted click-and-collect.
